sentences.text: Not every mark is telling you which side to pass on.
Some are saying something else, and you need to read those too.
Look at the three on screen.
The safe water mark has red and white vertical stripes, often a red ball on top, and a white light flashing Morse code A: short, long.
It means there’s good water all around it.
You’ll often find one at the seaward end of a channel.
The isolated danger mark is the opposite.
It’s black with red bands, with two black balls on top, and a white light flashing in groups of two.
It sits right on top of a small hazard, with safe water around it.
And the yellow special marks show things like anchorages, cable areas and spoil areas.
One more: a preferred channel mark has horizontal red and green bands.
